newsitem.title: USA: Slight May rise in US CPI shows inflation in check.
newsitem.headline: Slight May rise in US CPI shows inflation in check.

text.p: Consumer prices barely rose in May for a third straight month, restrained by the biggest drop in gasoline prices in six years as well as tumbling costs for tobacco and airline tickets, the government said Tuesday.

The Consumer Price Index rose 0.1 percent last month, the same as in April and March, the Labor Department said. The report gives the Federal Reserve added breathing room to refrain from raising interest rates when central bank policymakers meet July 1-2.

The bullish inflation news comes as the economy shows signs of a slowdown. That is considered good news for Fed officials worried that the torrid 5.8 percent growth rate in the first quarter of the year would unleash inflation.
The CPI showed that food prices rose 0.4 percent last month after falling 0.2 percent in April. Fruit prices fell 0.2 percent, but vegetable prices shot up 5.9 percent.

Energy prices fell 2.4 percent after falling 1.5 percent. The drop in energy prices was the largest since a 2.6 percent decrease in March 1991. Gasoline prices tumbled 4.1 percent, the biggest slide since a 4.6 percent drop in March 1991.
Airline fares fell 1.3 percent while automobile finance charges declined 2.5 percent, the biggest drop since a 2.8 percent slide in February 1992.
Tobacco prices fell 0.5 percent after rising 2.4 percent in April.
